vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: anfsf-v1
Version: 1.5.0

The ASF V4.0 skill bundle is a comprehensive governance and optimization module for OpenClaw, providing tools for veto enforcement, ownership verification, and economic modeling. It includes a dedicated security audit script (scripts/security-audit.sh) and a performance benchmarking suite (benchmarks/performance-benchmark.ts) to ensure code quality and operational efficiency. No indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration, unauthorized persistence, or harmful prompt injection were found; the code is well-structured, extensively documented, and aligns perfectly with its stated industrial governance purpose.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (governance, veto/ownership proofs, economics scoring, safe optimization) aligns with the files and runtime instructions; it doesn't request unrelated credentials, but it does integrate deeply with the agent (memory, agent status, security checks) so review the code and configs before enabling in production.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, declared tools, commands and the integrations (memory, agent-status, security-audit) are consistent with a governance/optimization skill. There are no requested environment variables or external credentials that don't fit the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and published docs instruct editing ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, running local CLI commands (clawhub, openclaw) and running the included security-audit script. Those actions are appropriate for installing a skill that integrates with the agent, but they give the skill (when enabled) ability to write into agent memory and extend agent status — behavior that should be expected for this kind of plugin but warrants review.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no automated install spec in SKILL.md, but the package includes TypeScript/Node source (index.ts, integrations/*.ts, benchmarks, scripts). That is coherent for a Node-based skill but means installation will require npm/ts-node/build steps not described in the simple instruction-only metadata; verify build/run steps and dependencies before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare or require any environment variables or external credentials. The documented operations (writing change events, ownership proofs, local audit) do not necessitate unrelated secrets. This is proportionate to the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced inclusion) and normal autonomous invocation are used. The skill integrates with persistent agent subsystems (Memory, Agent Status, Security checks) which is expected for governance tooling but increases its blast radius if misconfigured. Review what it writes to persistent memory and how long that data is retained.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a governance/optimization plugin that hooks into OpenClaw's memory, agent status, and security checks. Before enabling or publishing: (1) review the TypeScript sources (especially integrations/* and scripts/security-audit.sh) for any network calls, credential access, or unexpected file writes; (2) run the included security-audit script and npm audit locally in a sandboxed/dev agent, not production; (3) confirm build steps (Node >=20) and inspect package.json for dependencies; (4) verify what the memory schema will store and retention/visibility of stored events (the skill writes change events that may contain sensitive metadata); and (5) enable in a restricted/test agent first and limit optimizer/autonomous features until you’ve validated behavior. If you’re not comfortable auditing the code, ask a developer or security engineer to review the repository before enabling in production.
